rationale: Both candidates converge on the same diff-grounded issues (recipe FL2VA/Ref2VA copy-paste bug, fragile device_module binding at construction, allowlist widened beyond the stated CUDA/MUSA scope, and unverifiable test-coverage claims), giving them similar recall against the sparse ground truth (which centers on a platform-abstraction suggestion and a UT-reduction request that neither fully matches). X pulls ahead on precision and stakes: it identifies that `torch.random.fork_rng()` defaults `device_type` to "cuda" independent of the `devices` list, meaning the save/restore never actually touches the MUSA generator — a serious, technically verified correctness bug that directly contradicts the recipe's "restores both CPU and MUSA RNG states" claim. Y misses this entirely and lands on 'Approve with minor follow-ups,' a verdict that looks materially wrong if X's finding holds, so X is the stronger, better-calibrated review.
